title: "CLI reference"
---

*Reference: CLI · [Front matter](frontmatter.qmd) · [Cell options](cell-options.qmd) · [Configuration](configuration.qmd) · [Shortcodes](shortcodes.qmd) · [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd)*

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `preview <file.qmd> [port]` | Live preview server (default port 4321; aliases `dev`, `serve`) |
| `preview <dir>` | Live **multi-page site/book** preview (cross-page nav + per-page hot reload) |
| `build <file.qmd> [out.html]` | Write a self-contained HTML file (default `<name>.html`) |
| `build <file.qmd> --out <dir>` | Write `<dir>/index.html` + copied assets (a portable folder) |
| `build <file.qmd> --bare` | Write a **bare** page: zero `<script>`, zero CDN, CSS-only theme (drafts / archives / print input) |
| `build <dir> [--out <dir>]` | Build a **multi-page site/book** to `_site/` / `_book/` |
| `render <file.qmd>` | Render a one-shot full HTML page to stdout |
| `blocks <file.qmd>` | List block ids and sourcepos (for debugging) |
| `schema [--out <dir>]` | Emit the bundled JSON Schemas for `_site.yml` + front matter (editor autocomplete) |
| `check <file.qmd\|dir> [--format human\|json]` | List every located diagnostic and exit non-zero if any (a CI / pre-publish gate) |
| `init [dir]` | Scaffold a minimal previewable site (`_site.yml` + `index.qmd`) in `dir` (default `.`); refuses to overwrite |

`check` renders the document or site in memory and reports everything that flows
through the diagnostics channel: unknown front-matter / `_site.yml` / cell-option /
container keys (with did-you-mean), unknown callout kinds, broken `@xref`
cross-references, unknown shortcodes, a missing `bibliography:`, duplicate heading
`{#id}`s, broken in-page `#anchor` links, and opt-in `prose-lint:` findings. It also
catches these **publish-blocking** mistakes:

| Rule | Flags |
|---|---|
| Broken relative link | A `[text](other.qmd)` / `[text](page.html#x)` whose **local target file** is missing. In a site, links resolve against the page registry (`.qmd`→`.html`), so a cross-page anchor `page.html#frag` whose `frag` is no id on that page is flagged too. **External `http(s)://` links are never checked**: `check` stays offline and deterministic, and a `{{< embed >}}` deck or a cross-book / mounted link (one that climbs above the site root) is left alone. |
| Missing local video | A `{{< video clip.mp4 >}}` (or a raw `<video src>` / `<video><source></video>`) whose local file is absent (the video sibling of the local-image check). `<audio>` sources are skipped (often streamed/generated). |
| Dangling reactive input | A `{js}` cell's `//\| input: x` that no `{js}` cell (`//\| name`/`//\| viewof`) or `{{< input >}}` control defines, with a did-you-mean over the known names. Suppressed when the doc has a Python/R cell (a runtime `ojs_define` may publish the name). |
| Reactive dependency cycle | A loop among `{js}` cells (`a` consumes `b`, `b` consumes `a`), statically mirroring the runtime graph so none would run. |
| Heading-level skip | A heading that jumps two or more levels deeper than the one before it (an `h2` directly followed by an `h4`, skipping `h3`), which breaks the document outline for screen readers. Only a true *mid-document* skip is flagged (never "doesn't start at `h1`"), and slide decks are skipped (they are slide-structured). The static half of the live preview's a11y audit. |
| Missing alt text | A hand-written / passthrough `<img>` with no `alt` attribute, so a screen reader can't describe it (a decorative image should set `alt=""`). Markdown `![…](…)` always emits an `alt`, so this catches raw `<img>` only. |
| No accessible name | An `<a href>` / `<button>` in content with empty text and no `aria-label` / `title` / labelled image (e.g. an icon-only link), which a screen reader announces as just "link" / "button". |

It does **not** execute code cells (it is fast, kernel-free,
and deterministic, so runtime cell errors stay in `preview`/`build`). Output is
`path:line: message` by default, or a `[{file, line, message}]` array with
`--format json`. It exits `0` when clean and `1` when any diagnostic is found, so it
drops straight into CI or a pre-commit hook:

```sh
qmd-fast check .                          # fails (exit 1) if any page has a diagnostic
qmd-fast check . --format json > problems.json
```

`--format json` stays valid JSON even when `check` itself can't run: an unreadable or
missing path (or an empty site) is reported as a single `{"error": "…"}` object on
**stdout** (with a non-zero exit), so `qmd-fast check x --format json | jq` never chokes
on a stray human message. Human format keeps that error on stderr. Pointing `check` at a
directory that has a `_quarto.yml` but no `_site.yml` reports a migration breadcrumb
(qmd-fast uses the flat-native `_site.yml`, not Quarto's `_quarto.yml`) rather than a
confusing `no _site.yml`; `build` logs the same breadcrumb.

At a glance, here is everything `check` looks at, grouped by what it protects:

| Category | Catches |
|---|---|
| **Config typos** | Unknown front-matter, `_site.yml`, cell-option, and `:::` container keys (with did-you-mean), unknown callout kinds, unknown shortcodes, YAML parse errors |
| **Cross-references** | Broken `@fig-` / `@sec-` / `@eq-` / `@lst-` / `@tbl-` refs (no matching label), a citation with no `bibliography:` |
| **Links & anchors** | Broken relative `.qmd`/`.html` links (and, in a site, cross-page links + cross-page `#anchor`s), broken in-page `#anchor`s, duplicate heading `{#id}`s |
| **Local media** | Missing local images (`src`/`href`) and `{{< video >}}`/`<video>` files |
| **Reactive `{js}`** | A `//\| input:` naming nothing that's defined, a dependency cycle among `{js}` cells |
| **Accessibility** | An `<img>` with no `alt`, a mid-document heading-level skip (decks exempt), an `<a>`/`<button>` with no accessible name |
| **Opt-in** | `prose-lint:` banned-word findings |

External `http(s)://` links are never fetched (`check` stays offline and
deterministic), and it never executes code cells. On its own, `check` exits `1` if it
finds **anything** in any of those categories; it is the kernel-free gate.

`--strict` is a separate flag on **`build`** (not on `check`). It promotes a normally
non-fatal build into a hard failure: the page is still written, but `build` exits
non-zero if **any located warning** fired or **any code cell errored** at runtime.
Because `build` does run cells, `--strict` adds the one thing `check` structurally
can't see (a cell that *throws*) on top of the located diagnostics, which makes
`qmd-fast check . && qmd-fast build . --strict` a thorough two-stage CI gate: `check`
fails fast and kernel-free on structure, then a strict `build` proves every cell
actually runs.

`--version` / `-V` prints the version followed by the git commit it was built from,
in parentheses:

```text
qmd-fast 0.2.0 (cdf0a13)
```

`--help` / `-h` (or no arguments) prints the
top-level usage. Putting `--help` / `-h` **after** a subcommand
(`qmd-fast build --help`, `qmd-fast check -h`, …) prints a focused page for just that
command: its synopsis, its flags, and a one-line example. If
the default port (or one you pass) is already in use, `preview` auto-picks the next free
port and logs the chosen URL.

`preview` takes these flags (they may appear anywhere on the line):

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--host` | Bind your LAN and print a **QR code** for phones, gated by a per-session access token (see below) |
| `--open` | Launch the default browser at the preview URL |
| `--no-exec` | Render code cells as source without executing them (preview untrusted docs safely) |

`build` takes these flags (they may appear anywhere on the line):

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--out <dir>` (alias `--dir`) | Write a portable `<dir>/index.html` + copied assets instead of a single file |
| `--strict` | Exit non-zero if any cell errored or any located warning fired (a CI gate; the page is still written) |
| `--bare` | Single-doc only: emit a **bare** page (zero `<script>`, zero CDN, CSS-only theming) |
| `--jobs <N>` (alias `-j`) | Maximum pages to build in parallel (default: auto, memory- and core-capped; `--jobs 1` forces sequential; `--jobs 0` same as auto) |

A regular `build` already content-gates the optional enhancer scripts (mermaid, `{js}`,
walkthrough, tabset, scrolly) to the constructs a page actually uses, so a prose page
ships less JavaScript without losing any feature. `--bare` goes further for a
single document: it ships **no** `<script>` at all and themes purely with CSS (a forced
`theme:` is hard-coded; otherwise it follows the OS via `prefers-color-scheme`).
Server-rendered math still works; `{js}` cells, Mermaid rendering, and the
copy/lightbox/reader controls are dropped (each warned, never silently). A slide deck or
a `<dir>` site is refused (their navigation needs JavaScript). A `build` skips code
execution only through the `QMD_FAST_NO_EXEC=1` environment variable, not a `--no-exec`
flag.

A `--bare` page is still **responsive**: the viewport meta tag and every CSS media
query ship as usual, so it reflows on a phone and respects `prefers-color-scheme`. It
just has no behaviour that needs scripting. Because `{js}` cells and Mermaid both
render in the browser, a `--bare` build empties them (and warns once per kind) rather
than shipping a broken placeholder, so reach for `--bare` on prose, math, and
server-executed figures, not on pages built around live `{js}` or diagrams.

## Inspecting a document: `render` and `blocks`

Two commands print to a terminal instead of starting a server, which is handy for
piping, diffing, and debugging.

`render` writes one complete, self-contained HTML page to **stdout**. It is the
non-interactive twin of a single-file `build`, so you can redirect or pipe it:

```sh
qmd-fast render post.qmd > post.html
qmd-fast render post.qmd | grep -c data-block-id   # count emitted blocks
```

Unlike `build` and `preview`, `render` **never starts a kernel**: `{python}` and
`{r}` cells emit as highlighted source with an empty output block (no plots, and any
`@fig-` reference to a computed figure dangles), so it warns when it sees kernel cells:

```text
warn: render does not execute code cells (2 kernel cells emitted as source;
      figures/outputs will be empty). Use `build` or `preview` to run them.
```

`{js}` cells are fine, since they run in the browser. Use `build`/`preview` when you
need the executed outputs.

`blocks` is a debug view of the block model: for each block it prints the
content-hash id, the `line:col-line:col` sourcepos, the origin file (`(primary)` or
an `{{< include >}}`d path), and a 64-character text preview of the rendered HTML.
It does not execute anything. The shape is one aligned row per block:

```text
title: Some("Hello")
3 block(s)

id                sourcepos       source-file             preview
a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8  1:1-1:14        (primary)               Hello
0f9e8d7c6b5a4039  3:1-5:32        (primary)               A short paragraph that introduces…
7c6b5a4039f0e1d2  7:1-9:3         _includes/note.qmd      Note: included from another file
```

This is the same `data-block-id` + `data-sourcepos` that drive click-to-source and
incremental updates, so `blocks` is the way to confirm a block carries the source map
you expect (and which file it came from) without opening the browser dev tools.

`--host` binds `0.0.0.0`, so it gates non-loopback access behind a token baked into
the printed LAN URL and QR (`?t=…`, then a `qmd_token` cookie); a fresh token is
minted each server start, and loopback (`127.0.0.1`) is exempt. See
[Reading on any screen](../using/preview.qmd) for the full behaviour.

A `qmd-fast` launcher on `PATH` (`~/.local/bin/qmd-fast`) rebuilds the release
binary when the tool's sources change, then runs it, so `qmd-fast preview <file>`
works from anywhere.

## Environment

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `QMD_FAST_PYTHON` | Python with `ipykernel` for `{python}` cells (default `python3`) |
| `QMD_FAST_R` | R with `IRkernel` for `{r}` cells (default `R`) |
| `QMD_FAST_CELL_TIMEOUT` | Per-cell wall-clock cap in seconds before interrupt (default 120; `0` disables the cap, but a per-output silent-hang backstop still applies) |
| `QMD_FAST_HOST` | Same as `--host` (expose on the LAN) |
| `QMD_FAST_OPEN` | Same as `--open` (launch a browser) |
| `QMD_FAST_NO_EXEC` | Same as `--no-exec` (never execute code cells) |
| `QMD_FAST_NO_CACHE` | Ignore and skip writing the `_freeze/` execution cache |
| `QMD_FAST_NO_CLEAR` | Don't clear the terminal on each render (keep scrollback) |
| `QMD_FAST_MERMAID_URL` | Override the Mermaid library URL (self-host next to your site for a fully offline build; on load failure a visible `[data-mermaid-error]` banner shows the diagram source) |

Without a kernel, cells render as highlighted source and the preview shows a
"kernel unavailable" diagnostic rather than failing.
